text: Reading Passage 2 has six paragraphs, A-F.
Choose the most suitable headings for paragraphs A, B and D from the list of headings below.

list: Amazonia as unable to sustain complex societies
The role of recent technology in ecological research in Amazonia
The hostility of the indigenous population to North American influences
Early research among the Indian Amazons
The influence of prehistoric inhabitants on Amazonian natural history
The great difficulty of changing local attitudes and practices

items.items: The prehistoric inhabitants of Amazonia were relatively backward in technological terms. <input=NO>

items: The reason for the simplicity of the Indian way of life is that Amazonia has always been unable to support a more complex society.
There is a crucial popular misconception about the human history of Amazonia.
There are lessons to be learned from similar ecosystems in other parts of the world.
Most ecologists were aware that the areas of Amazonia they were working in had been shaped by human settlement.
The indigenous Amazonian Indians are necessary to the well-being of the forest.
It would be possible for certain parts of Amazonia to support a higher population

items.title: In 1942 the US anthropology student concluded that the Siriono
options: had had their way of life destroyed by invaders.
had only recently made permanent settlements.

items.title: The author believes recent discoveries of the remains of complex societies in Amazonia
options: are evidence of early indigenous communities.
are the remains of settlements by invaders.
are the ruins of communities established since the European invasions.
show the region has only relatively recently been covered by forest.

items.title: The assumption that the tropical ecosystem of Amazonia has been created solely by natural forces
options: has often been questioned by ecologists in the past.
has been shown to be incorrect by recent research.
was made by Peter Feinsinger and other ecologists.
has led to some fruitful discoveries.

items.title: The application of our new insights into the Amazonian past would
options: warn us against allowing any development at all.
cause further suffering to the Indian communities.
change present policies on development in the region.
reduce the amount of hunting, fishing, and 'slash-and-burn'.
